result.text: Title: Building a custom machine out of Lego bricks When building a custom machine out of Lego bricks, you first need to develop the basic design.
After that, you order certain Lego brick sets.
You give the lego sets to a group of children which should sort the parts for you (into a number of containers).
Your machine is built out of a number of subcomponents.
You build them individually, using parts from the sorted containers.
If there are no more parts in a container, you reorder individual parts.
After building each subcomponent, you have to test them individually and (if each test is successful) assemble them.
If subcomponents are not tested successfully, you have to redesign and rebuild them.

Title: Building a custom machine out of Lego bricks

When building a custom machine out of Lego bricks, you first need to develop the basic design.
After that, you order certain Lego brick sets.
You give the lego sets to a group of children which should sort the parts for you (into a number of containers).
Your machine is built out of a number of subcomponents.
You build them individually, using parts from the sorted containers.
If there are no more parts in a container, you reorder individual parts.
After building each subcomponent, you have to test them individually and (if each test is successful) assemble them.
If subcomponents are not tested successfully, you have to redesign and rebuild them.

result.rule: Several unconditional outgoing flows from one activity can all proceed. Use a gateway when the description requires a decision or synchronization.
Model every distinct activity, event, participant, decision, branch, loop, message and outcome stated in the description. Do not invent process facts.
Allow multiple start or end events when the description has distinct triggers or outcomes. Do not force all outcomes into one end.
Represent each modeled internal workflow with bpmn:process. Use isExecutable=false unless execution-ready behavior is explicitly required and fully specified.
Use an event-based gateway when the first occurring event selects the path. Target supported catching events or receive tasks, not ordinary tasks.
Use a boolean formal conditionExpression on a conditional flow only when the description supports the condition.

result.rule: When the description makes a later activity depend on the outcome of an evaluation and specifies a different response for the other outcome: model an exclusive gateway before the later activity to route each outcome to its corresponding path

When the description says an optional activity may occur after an outcome, and each occurrence is followed by another specified activity: Model the optional activity as a task on one branch of an exclusive gateway, with the other branch ending or continuing as described; connect the activity back to the specified later activity when it must follow each occurrence.

When the description says an activity may or may not occur before a later required activity: model the optional activity as one branch of an exclusive gateway, and merge the branches before the later required activity

When the description says to check whether required items are available and specifies a follow-up if any are unavailable: Model the check as an exclusive decision gateway with conditional flows for the available and unavailable outcomes, routing the unavailable outcome to the stated corrective activity.
